definitions.explanation: A person who has reached an exceptionally high level of skill or mastery in a particular field or art. Implies years of dedicated practice and deep expertise.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{料理|りょうり}の{達人|たつじん}だ。
examples.english: He is a master of cooking.

examples.japanese: {節約|せつやく}の{達人|たつじん}として{本|ほん}を{出|だ}した。
examples.english: She published a book as a savings expert.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{修行|しゅぎょう}を{経|へ}て、{剣|けん}の{達人|たつじん}と{呼|よ}ばれるようになった。
examples.english: After years of training, he came to be called a master swordsman.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{達人|たつじん} implies a level of mastery beyond ordinary expertise. It can be used seriously (martial arts, traditional crafts) or more casually (cooking, saving money) in modern Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {達人|たつじん}の{技|わざ} (a master's technique)
- {達人|たつじん}に{学|まな}ぶ (to learn from a master)
- 〜の{達人|たつじん} (a master of...)

The word appears in popular culture through the rhythm game {太鼓|たいこ}の{達人|たつじん} (Taiko no Tatsujin, "Taiko Master").

SIMILAR WORDS:
{名人|めいじん} (master, champion) is similar but is also used as a formal title, especially in traditional games like shogi and go. {達人|たつじん} emphasizes the person's skill level rather than a title.
